newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says investment plans quadruple.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says investment plans quadruple.

text.p: Investors notified the Egyptian government in December 1996 and January 1997 of plans to invest capital of 3,289 million pounds ($970 million) compared with notifications totalling 883 million in the same period one year earlier.

The government's General Organisation of Investment (GOFI) said in a statement on Friday that the total investment value of schemes covered by the applications, including credit from banks and other institutions, rose even faster -- by 398 percent to 7,478 million pounds from 1,501 million.
The figures reflect the intentions of investors rather than real spending. It can take years for the projects to come to fruition and some of them never see the light of day.

Ibrahim Fawzi, the secretary general of GOFI, said the projects submitted in the two-month period would create 22,616 jobs, compared with 14,739 jobs in projects submitted in December 1995 and January 1996.
He said the number of new jobs had increased at a relatively low rate because the projects used advanced technology.

GOFI did not break the figures down into investment by Egyptians or non-Egyptians but government officials say the level of foreign investment interest in the country has risen rapidly over the past six months.
The government estimates that foreign direct investment in Egypt last year was at least $2 billion.
